02 • Master quick sheet

Köppen Climate Classification — Corrected Quick Sheet

Quick-reference sheet for A–E groups, dryness logic, rainfall seasonality and common climate symbols.
A — Tropical
All months have mean temperature ≥18°C. Then distinguish Af, Am and Aw/As using rainfall seasonality.
B — Dry
First calculate the aridity threshold. Then distinguish BW (desert) from BS (steppe), followed by h/k.
C — Temperate
Use coldest-month and warmest-month temperature thresholds, then f/w/s for rainfall seasonality.
D — Snow / Continental
Cold winters with at least one sufficiently warm month; f/w/s and a/b/c/d refine the type.
E — Polar
Warmest month below 10°C; ET = tundra, EF = ice cap.
H — Highland
Highland is often added in regional/adapted classifications for complex mountain climates; it is not one of the five primary global Köppen groups.
02 • How to conclude

Decision Sequence

1. Temperature: Warmest month < 10°C → E. Every month ≥ 18°C → A. Otherwise continue.
2. Dryness: Test whether precipitation is low enough relative to temperature to qualify as B.
3. If B: Calculate Pₜₕ → BW if P < 0.5Pₜₕ; BS if 0.5Pₜₕ ≤ P < Pₜₕ.
4. If not B: Use coldest-month temperature to separate C and D.
5. Rainfall seasonality: f = no dry season; w = dry winter; s = dry summer.
6. Final: Combine the letters and then connect the code with the Indian region shown on the map.
03 • Calculation

Dry Climate — BW / BS

Let P = annual precipitation (mm), T = annual mean temperature (°C).

≥ 70% of rain in summer: Pₜₕ = 20(T + 14) 30–70% in summer: Pₜₕ = 20(T + 7) < 30% in summer: Pₜₕ = 20T P < 0.5 × Pₜₕ → BW = desert 0.5 × Pₜₕ ≤ P < Pₜₕ → BS = steppe B suffix: h → annual mean T ≥ 18°C k → annual mean T < 18°C

Worked example

T = 25°C, P = 180 mm, 75% summer rainfall
Pₜₕ = 20(25 + 14) = 780 mm
0.5Pₜₕ = 390 mm
180 < 390 → BW
25°C ≥ 18°C → h
Therefore: BWh.

Indian Köppen Codes

CodeCommon Indian descriptionBroad location
AwTropical savannaLarge parts of peninsular/central India
AmwTropical monsoon with short dry seasonHumid tropical/west-coast areas in traditional Indian maps
AsTropical climate with dry summerCoromandel/Tamil Nadu in the classic Indian adaptation
BShwSemi-arid / steppeNorth-western dry belt and adjoining areas
BWhwHot desertExtreme western Rajasthan / Thar
CwgMonsoon climate with dry winter in the Indian adaptationLarge northern plains in traditional maps
DfcCold humid winter / short summer typeHigher Himalayan areas in traditional maps

Exam caution: Different editions and modern Köppen-Geiger datasets can show more detailed subtypes. If an SSC question gives a particular map/table, use its stated convention.
05 • India reasoning

How the map can be understood

Thar / western Rajasthan

Very low precipitation relative to high thermal demand → B climate; desert test → BW; hot → h.

NW transition belt

More precipitation than desert but still dry relative to temperature → BS; hot → h.

Peninsular interior

Hot all year + pronounced seasonal dry period → commonly Aw.

Tamil Nadu / Coromandel

Rainfall seasonality differs because the northeast/retreating monsoon is important → As in the classic Indian adaptation.

Ganga plain

Monsoonal summer rainfall + winter dryness → Cwg in traditional Indian Köppen maps.

Himalayas

Altitude lowers temperature; higher elevations move toward D and E categories.
06 • SSC traps

Don't make these mistakes

Annual rainfall alone decides B?

No. Dryness is relative to temperature and seasonal rainfall distribution.

w means wet winter?

No. w means a dry winter.

s means summer rainfall?

No. s indicates a dry summer.

Every high-rainfall tropical place is Af?

No. The driest-month criterion matters.

Entire Rajasthan has one Köppen type?

No. Climate varies spatially; the desert core and transition areas need not have identical codes.

1. Which major Köppen group is defined by mean temperature of at least 18°C in every month?

2. In the standard Köppen notation, what does “w” indicate?

3. A climate has T = 25°C, P = 180 mm, and 75% of rainfall in summer. Which major dry class results?

4. Which code is commonly used for the hot desert belt of western Rajasthan in traditional Indian Köppen maps?

5. Which code represents tropical rainforest when every month is ≥18°C and the driest month receives at least 60 mm?

6. Which statement best explains why a location can be classified as BW rather than BS?

7. In the classic Indian Köppen adaptation, which code is associated with the Coromandel/Tamil Nadu dry-summer pattern?

8. If the warmest month's mean temperature is below 10°C, which major group should be considered first?

9. Which sequence is the correct way to solve a Köppen identification question?

10. Which major factor helps explain the movement from C/D climates toward E climates in the Himalayas?
